extracted.intended_audience: American colonists and political leaders considering independence; the general reading public
extracted.subtask_description: A political pamphlet giving prescriptive arguments and practical recommendations for declaring independence from Britain and for organizing national defence, government, and finance. Offers policy criteria and procedural advice for nation-building in the context of the American Revolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: National debt acceptable as national bond
rubrics_metrics.description: No nation ought to be without a debt. A national debt is a national bond; and when it bears no interest, is in no case a grievance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Britain's large national debt and its navy as compensation—argues that debt incurred to create public goods (like a navy) is not a grievance. Compares British figures and navy costs to show debt can be productive rather than harmful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest public borrowing in building a navy
rubrics_metrics.description: We ought to view the building a fleet as an article of commerce... 'Tis the best money we can lay out. A navy when finished is worth more than it cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that spending to build a navy is a sound national investment: ships can be sold if not needed, proceeds convert paper currency into specie, and a finished navy unites commerce and protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use domestic natural resources to supply naval construction
rubrics_metrics.description: No country on the globe is so happily situated, or so internally capable of raising a fleet as America. Tar, timber, iron, and cordage are her natural produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts America's natural advantages with countries that must import materials (e.g., Dutch). Builds the case that domestic industry can meet naval supply needs and make shipbuilding a national manufactory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manning strategy: train landsmen with a few able sailors
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not necessary that one-fourth part should be sailors... A few able and social sailors will soon instruct a sufficient number of active landsmen in the common work of a ship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by the privateer 'captain Death' who succeeded with few sailors; recommends using a small core of experienced seamen to make up crews from landsmen rather than relying entirely on professional sailors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localized naval force suffices versus a larger global navy
rubrics_metrics.description: If America had only a twentieth part of the naval force of Britain, she would be by far an over-match for her; because... our whole force would be employed on our own coast, where we should, in the long run, have two to one the advantage...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes home-coast advantage and the logistical limits on Britain's ability to project force globally; argues a smaller, locally-focused navy is strategically sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a peacetime naval reserve via merchant premiums
rubrics_metrics.description: If premiums were to be given to merchants to build and employ in their service ships mounted with twenty, thirty, forty, or fifty guns (the premiums to be in proportion to the loss of bulk to the merchant), fifty or sixty of those ships... would keep up a sufficient navy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes an economic incentive policy (premiums proportional to merchant loss) to merge commerce and defence, avoiding the English problem of a large idle peacetime fleet rotting in docks.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Continental charter as a solemn bond protecting rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A charter is to be understood as a bond of solemn obligation, which the whole enters into, to support the right of every separate part, whether of religion, professional freedom, or property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends a formal continental charter as a guarantee of individual and sectional rights; frames the charter as foundational and binding for future governance ('A firm bargain and a right reckoning make long friends').

rubrics_metrics.name: Government should protect freedom of conscience only
rubrics_metrics.description: As to religion, I hold it to be the indispensable duty of government to protect all conscientious professors thereof, and I know of no other business which government hath to do therewith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates limited government involvement in religion—protection for conscientious practitioners but no further governmental role; argues religious diversity is beneficial and should be tolerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large and equal representation essential
rubrics_metrics.description: The necessity of a large and equal representation; a small number of electors, or a small number of representatives, are equally dangerous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that small or unequal representation concentrates power and can let a few counties govern a province; gives Pennsylvania assembly example and cites Burgh for further reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carefully design methods for choosing Congress members
rubrics_metrics.description: Every well wisher to good order must own that the mode for choosing members of that body deserves consideration. And I put it as a question... whether representation and election is not too great a power for one and the same body of men to possess?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urges thoughtful institutional design for elections and representation, mindful of checks on concentrated power and the need to plan for posterity (virtue is not hereditary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid letting temporary expediencies become permanent oppressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediate necessity makes many things convenient, which, if continued would grow into oppressions. Expedience and right are different things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges that wartime measures (e.g., appointing delegates from assemblies) were necessary but cautions against making emergency arrangements permanent without regard to justice and right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare independence to enable foreign mediation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the custom of Nations, when any two are at war, for some other powers, not engaged in the quarrel, to step in as mediators... But while America calls herself the subject of Great Britain, no power... can offer her mediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that remaining a British subject prevents neutral powers from mediating; independence is required to enter diplomatic channels on an equal footing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare independence to secure foreign assistance and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: It is unreasonable to suppose that France or Spain will give us any kind of assistance, if we mean only to make use of that assistance for the purpose of repairing the breach... Under our present denomination of British subjects, we can neither be received nor heard abroad...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Makes the case that foreign powers will not aid or treat the Continent as a partner so long as it is officially British territory; independence is a precondition for meaningful alliances and trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish a manifesto to foreign courts explaining grievances
rubrics_metrics.description: Were a manifesto to be published, and despatched to foreign Courts, setting forth the miseries we have endured... declaring... we had been driven to the necessity of breaking off all connections with her... such a memorial would produce more good effects to this Continent than if a ship were freighted with petitions to Britain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates an explanatory diplomatic document to foreign courts to justify separation, assure peaceful intent, and open trade—preferred to sending petitions to Britain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act now: present time preferable for declaring independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The present time... is preferable to all others... the fewer our numbers are, the more land there is yet unoccupied... our military ability, at this time, arises from the experience gained in the last war, and which in forty or fifty years time would be totally extinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines demographic, economic (land availability), and military-experience arguments to argue for immediate action rather than delay which would make independence harder to achieve later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sale of public (back) lands to pay national debt and support government
rubrics_metrics.description: It is by the sale of those lands that the debt may be sunk, without burthen to any, and the quit-rent reserved thereon will always lessen, and in time will wholly support the yearly expense of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a fiscal policy: sell western/back lands to pay debts and reserve quit-rents as a perpetual revenue stream for government expenses; includes rough valuations and revenue estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form a charter before appointing rulers
rubrics_metrics.description: The articles or charter of government should be formed first, and men delegated to execute them afterwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural prescription to establish a constitution/charter first to avoid being later governed by a usurper or 'fortunate ruffian'; stresses starting government 'at the right end.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw clear legal distinctions between enemy prisoners and domestic insurgents
rubrics_metrics.description: A line of distinction should be drawn between English soldiers taken in battle, and inhabitants of America taken in arms. The first are prisoners, but the latter traitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for clear legal categories and punishments to preserve order and to avoid confusion from the current lack of law; implies need for codified legal definitions in a new government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on Britain for future protection after reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Can they be so unwise as to mean that she will keep a navy in our harbors for that purpose?... the power which hath endeavoured to subdue us, is of all others the most improper to defend us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that trusting a former aggressor to protect you is naïve—British protection could mask conquest; self-protection is preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use present social bonds (youth and misfortune) to create lasting union
rubrics_metrics.description: The intimacy which is contracted in infancy, and the friendship which is formed in misfortune, are of all others the most lasting and unalterable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends establishing union now while bonds forged in youth and shared hardship persist, warning that later commercial and sectional interests could divide the continent.
